subject: Banking
title: Basel Accords: Global Banking Rules
description: A quick, practical guide to Basel Accords: Global Banking Rules.

hook.text: The Basel Accords set global rules for how much cash banks must hold. Over 100 countries follow them.

buildup.text: Basel I in 1988 required banks to hold capital equal to 8% of their risk-weighted assets.

discovery.text: Basel II added risk sensitivity. Basel III, after 2008, raised capital requirements and added liquidity rules.

twist.text: Countries implement Basel at different speeds. Some water down the rules. Global standards become local compromises.

climax.text: Basel proves that banking regulation must be global because banking risk is global. But enforcement remains national.

punchline.text: Global rules, national enforcement. Banking regulation's permanent gap.

quiz.question: What do the Basel Accords require banks to do?
options: Hold minimum capital reserves relative to their risk

details.summary: The Basel Accords are international banking regulations that set minimum capital requirements, forcing banks worldwide to hold sufficient buffers against losses. Each iteration, from Basel I through Basel III, tightened rules after new crises exposed weaknesses.
details.whyItMatters: Basel rules determine how much risk banks can take globally. Every mortgage rate, business loan, and credit card limit is influenced by Basel capital requirements that banks must meet.
takeaways: Basel I in 1988 established the first international bank capital standards
Basel III after 2008 significantly increased capital and liquidity requirements
Implementation varies by country, creating regulatory arbitrage opportunities

faq.question: What are bank capital requirements?
faq.answer: Capital requirements mandate that banks fund a minimum percentage of their assets with shareholders' equity rather than borrowed deposits. This cushion absorbs losses before depositors are affected, strengthening bank resilience against downturns.

faq.question: Why does it take decades to implement Basel rules?
faq.answer: Banks lobby for weaker rules, countries implement at different speeds, and transition periods allow gradual compliance. Each Basel round takes years to negotiate and over a decade to fully implement, during which new risks may emerge.
